'''''Agave striata''''' is a plant species native to Northeastern [[Mexico]].<ref>CONABIO. 2009. Catálogo taxonómico de especies de México. 1. In Capital Nat. México. CONABIO, Mexico City.</ref><ref>Zuccarini, Joseph Gerhard. Novorum Actorum Academia Caesareae Leopoldinae-Carolinae Germanicae Naturae Curiosorum 16(2): 678. 1833.</ref> Because the species is widespread and does not appear to be under any significant threats, it is not considered by the [[IUCN]] to be threatened.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

==Description==
''A. striata''  forms [[Rosette (botany)|rosettes]] of hundreds of thin, narrow leaves, 60 cm (2 feet) long and 1.0 cm (0.4 inches) wide. The leaves stick straight out or arch gently upward toward the center of the plant, each ending in a very sharp, brown and black spine. The [[flower spike]] is up to 3 m (10 feet) tall and bears whitish yellow flowers 3.0-4.0 cm (1.2-1.6) inches in diameter. In the wild, numerous [[Suckers (botany)|suckers]] result in thick clusters of plants growing to form impenetrable thickets.<ref>Zdeněk Ježek & Libor Kunte. 2005. Complete Encyclopedia of Succulents. Rebo.</ref><ref>Bailey, L.H. & E.Z. Bailey. 1976. Hortus Third i–xiv, 1–1290. MacMillan, New York.</ref><ref>Gentry, H. S. 1982. Agaves of Continental North America i–xiv, 1–670. The University of Arizona Press, Tucson.</ref>
